memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Do not do any work on that day, because it is the Day of Atonement,
when atonement is made for you before the LORD your God. Those who do
not deny themselves on that day must be cut off from their people. I
will destroy from among their people anyone who does any work on that
day'" - Lev 23:28-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The warning is severe, and we should not soften it. Anyone who worked
on the Day of Atonement, or refused to humble themselves, was to be cut
off. This was covenant law given to a particular nation, not a rule for
society today - but the seriousness behind it still speaks.

Why such severity about working on that specific day? Because working
on the Day of Atonement would say something dreadful: that a person
thought they could contribute to their own forgiveness, or that they
did not need it.

Atonement was something done for you, not with you. The high priest
went in alone. The people simply waited, humbled, empty-handed.

Dear friend, this is the offence at the heart of grace. We want to
help. We want to bring something. And God says the work is done.

Paul writes that it is by grace you have been saved, through faith -
and this is not from yourselves, it is the gift of God, not by works,
so that no one can boast (Eph 2:8-9). From the cross Jesus said, "It is
finished" (John 19:30).

Stop working for what has already been given. Receive it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I still trying to add something to what Christ has finished?
2. What does it mean for me to rest in His completed work?
3. Where does pride make it hard for me to receive grace?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord Jesus, You said it is finished, and I believe You. Stop me from
adding my own efforts to Your perfect work, and let me simply receive.
Amen.
